comment: Drug-drug interaction table for tool/action combinations. Each row documents a REAL documented disaster. Add a row for every 'X + Y broke Z' you discover. check.py matches tool_name + serialised tool_input (and optional bg-registry state) against each row and injects harm + safe_alternative when a row fires.

rows.harm: Parallel file-disjoint subagents share one git index. 'git add -A' / 'git add .' / 'git add --all' sweeps sibling work-unit files into the wrong commit, silently contaminating unrelated branches. This has caused repeated commit-scope corruption in the metaswarm orchestrated workflow.
rows.safe_alternative: Use Agent(isolation:worktree) so each parallel subagent owns its own git index. If worktrees are not available, stage only specific files ('git add <file>') and run 'git diff --cached' to verify scope before committing.

rows.harm: Running a MITM proxy (mitmproxy/mitmdump) while Battle Cats also has its local .dat cache cleared corrupts BC's date state — the date-drift guard sub_525AB0 trips the HGT (Hack Guard Trap), applying a 99-day half-XP penalty that persists until recovery. The combination is HGT-orthogonal: the event injection goal is fine; the delivery method is the problem.
rows.safe_alternative: Patch event_0.dat in place: AES-128-ECB decrypt (key = md5('battlecats')[:8].hex), edit, re-encrypt, write back. Never run a live MITM proxy or clear BC cached .dat files while testing event injection.

rows.harm: The semgrep Pro engine (loaded via the plugin:semgrep MCP server) keeps approximately 920 MB of osemgrep-pro RESIDENT per session. With multiple concurrent Claude Code sessions the combined RSS exceeds available RAM, causing system-wide OOM. Confirmed on CC #28860.
rows.safe_alternative: Remove plugin:semgrep from .mcp.json and run the plain semgrep CLI (OSS engine) directly via Bash. If Pro-engine analysis is needed, isolate it to a single dedicated session and kill it when done.

rows.harm: A Frida Interceptor.attach on a high-frequency render-thread function (e.g. getGlobal) crashes the process on scene transitions: hooks are torn down under load and leave the process in a broken state. Confirmed crash vector in Battle Cats RE work.
rows.safe_alternative: Use a periodic JS write/poll pattern (setInterval reading a memory offset) or a one-shot patchCode instead of a per-frame Interceptor.attach hook. For sampling use Stalker, not per-frame interception.

rows.harm: MSYS/Git-Bash on Windows mistranslates /dev/ device paths for non-standard devices (e.g. /dev/sda, /dev/tty, Android ADB block devices). Redirecting output to such a path silently produces a 0-byte file instead of writing to the intended device, corrupting the target without any error.
rows.safe_alternative: Use native Windows write methods: PowerShell Set-Content / Out-File, or for ADB device writes use the 'cat > <path>' syntax inside an explicit 'adb shell' session preserving uid and SELinux context.

rows.harm: NEVER-ROTATE + split-brain: minting or auto-healing Databricks PATs (token/create, preemptive_rotate, health_monitor without --no-create-pat) burns the live harvest SQL PATs or falsely 'heals' Plane A while Plane B (dbx_crossws.ps1 ngo/alvaro) is still SCIM-200. Measured false ALL_METHODS_FAILED on clusters-first Plane A while warehouse harvest still worked.
rows.safe_alternative: Use retargeted health: python scripts/health_monitor.py --prefer-probe scim --no-create-pat (loads harvest PATs; probes both slots). If both SCIM fail, GEM-5 cookie-bridge last rung on isolated durable profile (databricks_cookie_bridge.py status/extract durable-only) — do not mint PAT, do not main-inject, do not Read cookie JSON or dbx_crossws.ps1 into chat; call scim_me_recheck.py / health_monitor instead. See HARVEST-RULES Plane C section.
